description: Background job queue for Go that stores jobs in the database you already use (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DynamoDB, Firestore, in-memory), with transactional enqueue (outbox pattern), typed futures that await a job's result, retries, cron, retention by default, an admin dashboard, OpenTelemetry, and deterministic test clocks.
rules: Import v2 paths: github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/v2 for the root and github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/driver/<name>/v2 for drivers
Use EnqueueTx (not Enqueue) when inside a database transaction — this is the transactional outbox pattern and guarantees the job appears only if the transaction commits
Use the in-memory driver (driver/memory) and gontest package for tests — no Docker or real database needed
To get a job's return value: var T = future.Define[Args, Result](); T.Register(registry, m, handler, opts); f := future.Bind(m, client, T); then f.Call(ctx, args), or f.Enqueue(ctx, args) and Await
future.Func.Call is one-shot: it deletes the job and result after returning a value. Pass the future.Manager as WorkerConfig.Observer for instant local wake-up
Use future.BindTx and EnqueueTx(ctx, tx, args) to enqueue a future inside a transaction; await only after commit, since a rolled-back job returns future.ErrNotFound

Worker pools prune old jobs by default (completed/cancelled 24h, discarded 7d, results 1h) through indexes Migrate creates; set WorkerConfig.Retention (goncordia.KeepForever keeps a state) or RetentionInterval: -1 to disable
Inject clock.Manual into the client, worker or scheduler, and driver in tests; Advance fires timers and tickers without sleeping

EnqueueTx works on Postgres, MySQL, SQLite (pgxv5, stdlib, gorm, bun), MongoDB, and Firestore; Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DynamoDB, and the in-memory driver reject it with driver.ErrUnsupported, so use Enqueue after commit there
Mount admin.New(driver) behind application authentication; it exposes mutating job and queue actions
MongoDB requires a replica set — standalone MongoDB will fail at New()
SQLite requires db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) — only one writer allowed
Firestore requires two composite indexes created manually on collection goncordia_jobs: queue ASC + state ASC + run_at ASC (fetching) and state ASC + finalized_at ASC (retention)
On Redis, use maxmemory-policy noeviction (or volatile-*); Migrate rejects allkeys-* because eviction can drop jobs and results
For MongoDB use driver/mongodbv2 (mongo-driver v2, transaction type *mongo.Session); driver/mongodb is deprecated

Retention metrics: goncordia.NewRetentionMetrics() as WorkerConfig.Observer (combine with goncordia.WorkerObservers) and admin.WithMetrics; otelgoncordia.Instrumentation records goncordia.retention.* metrics
